# Align "More to Customize" Container with Add/Edit Habit Screen

## Context

The Add/Edit Habit screen is composed of three top-level sections rendered in order:
1. `NameInputSection` — flat layout, centered hero heading + centered text input
2. `CustomizeSection` — flat layout, centered uppercase divider labels ("Choose an icon", "Pick a color") followed by their pickers
3. `AdvancedOptionsSection` ("More to Customize") — a **bordered card** with left-aligned icon + title row + count badge + chevron

Section 3's container language doesn't match sections 1 and 2:
- It is the only section wrapped in a bordered card (`borderWidth: 1`, `colors.border`)
- It is the only section with a left-aligned icon + bold inline title pattern
- It is the only section using a count badge
- Inner `AdvancedOptionRow` cards already do nested-card-on-card visuals, which look correct against the warm parchment background but inconsistent against the flat siblings above

Goal: bring the outer "More to Customize" container into the same visual language as `CustomizeSection` while preserving its collapse/expand affordance and the prominent entry point (May 21 work).

---

## Visual Mock — Before / After

### BEFORE (current)

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                    │
│            ━━━━━ drag handle ━━━━━                 │
│  Cancel              Edit your habit         Save  │
│                                                    │
│                  Edit your habit                   │
│                                                    │
│         ╭──────────────────────────────╮           │
│         │      Read 30 minutes         │           │
│         ╰──────────────────────────────╯           │
│                                                    │
│                 CHOOSE AN ICON                     │
│           [📖] [🏃] [🧘] [💧] [📚] [⭐]            │
│                                                    │
│                  PICK A COLOR                      │
│           ● ● ● ● ● ● ● ●                          │
│                                                    │
│         [ Daily reminder · 8:00 AM      ⏺ ]        │
│                                                    │
│  ╔════════════════════════════════════════════╗    │  ◄── bordered card,
│  ║ ⇋  More to customize           3   ⌄      ║    │     visually heavy,
│  ╚════════════════════════════════════════════╝    │     inconsistent with
│                                                    │     siblings above
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### AFTER (aligned)

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                    │
│            ━━━━━ drag handle ━━━━━                 │
│  Cancel              Edit your habit         Save  │
│                                                    │
│                  Edit your habit                   │
│                                                    │
│         ╭──────────────────────────────╮           │
│         │      Read 30 minutes         │           │
│         ╰──────────────────────────────╯           │
│                                                    │
│                 CHOOSE AN ICON                     │
│           [📖] [🏃] [🧘] [💧] [📚] [⭐]            │
│                                                    │
│                  PICK A COLOR                      │
│           ● ● ● ● ● ● ● ●                          │
│                                                    │
│         [ Daily reminder · 8:00 AM      ⏺ ]        │
│                                                    │
│             MORE TO CUSTOMIZE  ·  3            ⌄   │  ◄── matches sibling
│                                                    │     divider language
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### AFTER — Expanded

```
│             MORE TO CUSTOMIZE  ·  3            ⌃   │
│                                                    │
│   Tap any option below to customize how this       │
│   habit grows.                                     │
│                                                    │
│   🌱 Growth Type · Compounding · ~66-day build     │
│                                                    │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│   │ [♥] Strength Curve                  EDIT │     │
│   │     Forgiving · ~30-day build            │     │
│   │     How your habit's strength grows…     │     │
│   └──────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│   │ [🌱] Growth Icons                   EDIT │     │
│   │     Classic · 5 stages                   │     │
│   │     The 5-stage emoji progression…       │     │
│   └──────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│   │ [🎯] Streak Goal                    EDIT │     │
│   │     30-day target                        │     │
│   │     A motivational target — purely…      │     │
│   └──────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
```

Inner `AdvancedOptionRow` cards stay as-is — they now read correctly against the flat surface (same surface they already use: `colors.background` warm parchment) without competing with an outer bordered card.

---

## Specific Style Changes

File: `src/components/AdvancedOptions/AdvancedOptionsSection.tsx`

### 1. Drop the outer bordered card wrapper

Current outer `Animated.View` (lines 108-117):
```tsx
<Animated.View
  className='mx-6 mt-6 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl'
  ...
  style={{
    backgroundColor: colors.card,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: colors.border,
  }}
>
```

Replace with a flat container that matches `CustomizeSection`'s rhythm:
```tsx
<Animated.View
  className='mt-4 px-6'
  ...
  // no backgroundColor, no border — flat in the scroll flow
>
```

Rationale: `CustomizeSection` is wrapped externally in `px-6` by `HabitEditScreen` (line 113). Mirroring `px-6` here keeps the same content gutter. `mt-4` (16px) replaces `mt-6` (24px) because we no longer need extra breathing room to separate two competing card surfaces — the divider label provides the separation.

### 2. Reframe the pressable header as a section divider

Current header (lines 118-159) uses left-aligned `SlidersHorizontal` + body-weight title + caption "3" badge.

Replace with a centered uppercase divider label matching `CustomizeSection` (lines 50-60 of `CustomizeSection.tsx`):
```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityLabel='More to customize, 3 options'
  accessibilityRole='button'
  accessibilityState={{ expanded }}
  className='flex-row items-center justify-center gap-2 py-2'
  onPress={toggle}
>
  <Text
    className='uppercase'
    style={{
      ...typography.caption,
      fontWeight: fontWeights.semibold,
      letterSpacing: 0.5,
      color: colors.text.tertiary,
    }}
  >
    More to customize  ·  3
  </Text>
  <Animated.View style={chevronStyle}>
    <ChevronDown
      color={colors.text.tertiary}
      size={iconSizes.small}
      strokeWidth={2}
    />
  </Animated.View>
</Pressable>
```

Key changes:
- Typography mirrors `CustomizeSection` labels: `typography.caption` + `fontWeights.semibold` + `letterSpacing: 0.5` + `color: colors.text.tertiary` + `uppercase`
- "3" count merged inline with a middot, no separate badge
- Chevron stays as the affordance — interaction is preserved
- `SlidersHorizontal` icon removed; the chevron is sufficient signal once the label matches the rest of the screen

### 3. Expanded body — drop horizontal card padding

Current expanded container (line 162): `className='gap-2.5 px-3 pb-3'`

Update to: `className='gap-2.5 pb-2'`

Rationale: outer card padding is gone, so inner `AdvancedOptionRow`s sit at the full content width (already inside `px-6` from step 1). The inner row cards remain identical — they already render correctly at this width inside the screen.

The helper caption (lines 166-175) keeps its existing typography/color; remove the `paddingHorizontal: 4` since it's no longer compensating for inner padding.

The Growth Type pill (lines 176-202) keeps its existing styling but drop `marginLeft: 4` for the same reason — `self-start` now aligns to the new content edge.

---

## What Stays the Same

- Collapsed-by-default behavior (`useState(false)` at line 73)
- Chevron rotation animation (lines 75-84)
- Haptic feedback on toggle (line 87)
- `FadeIn`/`FadeOut` on expand/collapse content (lines 163-164)
- `LinearTransition` layout animation (line 111) — moves to new outer wrapper
- Inner `AdvancedOptionRow` styling — unchanged
- All three sheet modals at the bottom (lines 248-280) — unchanged
- Accessibility labels, roles, and state — unchanged

## Files Modified

- `src/components/AdvancedOptions/AdvancedOptionsSection.tsx` (only file)

No changes to:
- `AdvancedOptionRow.tsx` (rows render correctly as-is on the flat surface)
- `AdvancedOptionEditAffordance.tsx`
- `AdvancedSheet.tsx`
- `HabitEditScreen.tsx`
- `CustomizeSection.tsx`
- Theme/token files

## Verification

1. Open Add/Edit Habit modal (tap a habit on home, or "+" then existing habit)
2. Scroll to the bottom of the form — confirm "MORE TO CUSTOMIZE · 3" reads as a section divider matching "CHOOSE AN ICON" / "PICK A COLOR" above it (same case, weight, color, letterSpacing)
3. Tap the divider — chevron rotates, content expands with FadeIn, three option rows visible
4. Confirm option rows fill the content width with the same 24px gutter as siblings
5. Tap each row — corresponding sheet opens (algorithm, growth icons, streak goal)
6. Toggle dark mode — verify the divider label uses `colors.text.tertiary` correctly in both themes
7. Verify with VoiceOver: accessibility label still reads "More to customize, 3 options", state still announces collapsed/expanded
8. Confirm `npm run lint:max-lines` still passes (file is currently 283 lines and stays under threshold)

“More to Customize” — make the box obviously openable

Six variants ranked by tap-affordance strength. Each preserves the app’s warm-minimal language. The current pill reads as a label because it lives in the same horizontal band where sibling section labels (Choose an icon / Pick a color) are also centered and tertiary-colored — context kills its button-ness.

Why the current pill fails: centered uppercase tertiary text + a chevron looks like a passive header. Users skim and treat it like the labels above it. The fix is either change the shape so it can’t be mistaken for a header or show what’s inside so the value is visible before tap.

V1 · iOS settings row
Full-width row · trailing chevron

The pattern every iPhone user has tapped 10,000 times. Left icon, title + subtitle, chevron on the right. Unmistakably tappable.

PROS · zero learning curve, full-width tap target (~600px²), trailing chevron is the universal “opens-something” signal.
CONS · most visually heavy of the six; partly walks back the alignment work we just did.
V2 · Preview + Edit
Show what’s inside · with an Edit pill

Users see the current values as chips; the "Edit" pill makes it obviously interactive. Best for discoverability — they learn what's customizable without opening.

PROS · teaches users what's customizable before they tap, EDIT pill is unambiguous, preview chips reduce blind-tapping.
CONS · more visual density; if the section is collapsed by default the preview duplicates info that's about to expand.
V3 · Action pill
+ icon · primary color · verb-led

Compact like the current pill but borrows brand color and a plus-icon. "Customize" is a verb; the user expects something to happen on tap.

…reminder section above…

PROS · clearly a CTA, brand color breaks out of the gray-label trap, "+ Customize" reads as action.
CONS · borrows the primary color used by Save/CTA buttons — might compete with the Save button at the top.
V4 · Drawer affordance
Pull-handle on top · "Pull to reveal"

Mimics a physical drawer or bottom sheet. The handle visual is a known signal for "pull/open me." Closest to the iOS sheet pattern users already know.

…reminder section above…

PROS · the handle = "drag me open" schema, content list shows what's hidden, subtitle previews contents.
CONS · we don’t actually drag this open (just tap) — could over-promise interaction, and the handle is a new visual primitive in this app.
V5 · Dashed disclosure
Dashed border = "more here" · verb in label

Dashed outlines universally signal "expandable" or "incomplete." Combined with an emoji preview and a "Tap to customize" verb, intent is obvious.

CONS · introduces a new border style; dashed lines can feel un-polished if not done carefully.
V6 · Section + text button
Sibling-aligned label · "Customize" CTA on right

Keep the section header rhythm of "Choose an icon" / "Pick a color", but anchor a brand-colored "Customize ›" text-button on the right. Stays minimal; the CTA color carries the affordance.

…reminder section above…

8:00 AM

Strength curve · growth icons · streak goal

PROS · most aligned to existing sibling labels, CTA color does the heavy lifting, summary teases contents without opening.
CONS · two tap targets (button vs card) split the user's attention; brand-color CTA might compete with Save.

Recommendation: V1 (iOS settings row) for safety, V2 (Preview + Edit) for delight

V1 is the safest pick — it's the pattern users tap dozens of times a day in iOS Settings, so there's no learning curve and no risk of misreading it as a header. It walks back some of the visual minimalism we landed on, but the tradeoff is worth it for clarity.

V2 is the more interesting bet — it surfaces what's actually customizable (Forgiving · Classic · 30-day) as chips, so users learn the feature without tapping in. The EDIT pill removes any doubt that the card is interactive. Best long-term, but slightly more visual weight.

Skip V3 (color competes with Save), V4 (handle over-promises drag), V5 (dashed border introduces new primitive), V6 (split tap targets).

## Context

The current centered uppercase pill ("MORE TO CUSTOMIZE · 3 ⌄") looks too much like the non-interactive section labels above it (CHOOSE AN ICON, PICK A COLOR). Users skim past it as a passive header rather than tapping. We need a container that reads as an interactive tile — without going back to the heavy bordered card we just moved away from.

V2 surfaces what's actually inside the section as preview chips (♥ Forgiving · 🌱 Classic · 🎯 30-day) and adds an EDIT pill (the same green pill pattern already used on the inner option rows). Two wins: (1) the chips + pill make the tile obviously interactive, and (2) users learn what the section contains before they decide to tap in.

“More to Customize” — V2 polish variations

Same core idea (preview what's inside + tile-wide tap target) but six variations on visual treatment. The goal: make the tile feel meaningful and obviously interactive without dragging back the heaviness of the original bordered card.

What's wrong with the current build: the tile uses colors.card (warm stone) on a background that's also warm stone — they blend. Chips use the same warm tone, so they disappear into the tile. The result reads as one washed-out blob instead of a clear tap target with crisp preview content.
A · Elevated white card
Lift the surface, keep the chip layout

Same V2 structure, but the tile is white with a subtle shadow so it floats above the warm background. Chips get a soft warm fill to stand out against the white.

B · Tinted color chips
Each chip earns its own color tint

Chips inherit semantic colors from the inner option rows: strength curve = warm red (heart), icons = primary green, streak goal = amber. Instant visual association.

My picks: B (color-tinted chips) or E (mini-row preview)

B is the most surgical fix — keep everything we already shipped but give chips real color tints so they look like preview tags instead of washed-out labels. Each chip's color matches the inner option row's icon background, so users will recognize them. Five-minute change.

E is the more ambitious bet — a full preview of what's inside, ending with a primary green CTA button. This is the variant where the user cannot miss that it's interactive, and they learn the feature without expanding. Bigger footprint but worth it.

Skip A (too small a leap), C (too busy with the leading icon), D (loses the chips you liked), F (circular-arrow primitive is overkill).
